claims.quote: Total operating expenses were $401.6K, up 9.7% from September.
claims.why: All accounts went from $365,966.96 to $401,554.37: +$35,587.41, +9.7%. No cause is stated.

claims.quote: Locum costs of $28.8K are new this month, covering Dr. Alvarez's leave.
claims.why: Locum tenens went from $0.00 to $28,800.00: four weekly Summit Locums invoices of $7,200 for Dr. Ingram 'for Dr. Alvarez'. The sentence states a level that is also the change, since September was zero.

claims.quote: Provider compensation was down about $18K with Dr. Alvarez on leave.
claims.why: Provider compensation went from $115,400.00 to $106,200.00: -$9,200.00, not -$18K (about twice the real fall). Dr. Alvarez's pay did fall $18,800, but the quarterly Q3 quality incentive ($9,600) paid on 10/31 offsets half of it.

claims.quote: Clinical wages were up 5% on overtime for the Saturday flu clinics.
claims.why: Clinical wages went from $76,828.09 to $80,783.90: +$3,955.81, +5.1%. Saturday flu clinic overtime was $900 in September and $4,750 in October: +$3,850, 97% of the change.

claims.quote: Payroll taxes and benefits eased about $1.2K with Dr. Alvarez off payroll.
claims.why: Payroll taxes & benefits went from $29,956.68 to $28,799.85: -$1,156.83. Employer taxes on Dr. Alvarez fell from $1,426.00 to $260.40 (-$1,165.60), 101% of the change. 'Eased' is the direction word.

claims.quote: Vaccines were up $13K as the second, larger flu pre-book shipment landed in October.
claims.why: Vaccines went from $27,730.29 to $40,930.63: +$13,200.34. Flu pre-book shipment 1 ($21,600) was in September and shipment 2 ($34,800) in October: +$13,200, 100% of the change.

claims.quote: Lab fees fell $12.5K, entirely the clean-up of September's duplicate Valley Reference invoice.
claims.why: Lab fees went from $12,800.00 to $300.00: -$12,500.00. Invoice 88213 ($6,400) was posted twice in September and credited in October (-$6,400): the duplicate accounts for -$12,800 of the change (102%); the regular monthly bill rose $300.

claims.quote: Medical supplies were up $3.1K on the new sharps disposal program.
claims.why: Medical supplies went from $6,865.13 to $6,716.46: -$148.67. The sharps mail-back program ($3,100) is real but is booked to Medical Waste & Janitorial, which rose exactly $3,100.

claims.quote: Billing service fees rose $2.3K due to the clearinghouse price increase.
claims.why: Billing service went from $15,669.50 to $17,993.00: +$2,323.50, so the amount is right. No transaction is a clearinghouse charge or price change: the rate is still 5.5%, applied to higher September collections ($312,600 vs $284,900, +$1,523.50), plus an $800 credentialing fee.

claims.quote: EHR and IT were up roughly $3.6K: the one-time patient portal implementation, net of a service credit for September's network outage.
claims.why: EHR & IT went from $5,839.00 to $9,439.00: +$3,600.00. Portal implementation $4,500 less the Bluestone SLA credit $900 = $3,600, exactly the change.

claims.quote: Med mal rose $770 on the October 1 renewal.
claims.why: Malpractice went from $9,350.00 to $10,120.00: +$770.00, the monthly amortisation of the new 26-27 policy against the old one. Immaterial (below $1,000).

claims.quote: CME rose $3.2K for Dr. Kim's trip to the FMX conference.
claims.why: Continuing education went from $150.00 to $3,395.00: +$3,245.00. FMX registration $1,195, airfare $640 and hotel $1,410 for Dr. Kim = $3,245, 100%.

non_claims.quote: Visits were 4,180 for the month, up 6%, and September collections of $312.6K were our best this year.
non_claims.why: Visits and collections are not expense accounts.

non_claims.quote: We will budget locum coverage through mid-January.
